turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish child, what a sorry excuse is this! You think a little trouble with your sister is a sufficient reason for disobeying me?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I am very sorry, Miss Havisham, but I am afraid I don't know where Estella is, and I didn't want to go out of the room and leave you alone.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I am afraid, Miss Havisham, that I did not mean to hurt your feelings or disobey you, and I shall try to make it up to you by being more pleasant if you would be so kind as to give me a little time.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I don't know if I'm worthy of your notice, Miss Havisham, but I must confess that I'm a little overwhelmed by your grandeur.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will play with me, Pip, just as you would play with Estella. I will not be ignored.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will play with me, Pip, or leave my house at once. I will not be trifled with.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I am afraid, Miss Havisham, that I am not used to playing with ladies of your quality, and I fear I might not be able to play in a way that would please you.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I don't know what to play, Miss Havisham, or how I could possibly play with you, as you would play with Estella.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will play with me, Pip, because I say so. I will not be denied.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Silence is a luxury I afford few, Pip. Speak, and tell me what games you think suitable for a lady of my... distinction.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm not sure I'm the right person for playing games with you, Miss Havisham, as I'm a very simple and uneducated boy, and I fear I would not be able to hold your attention for long.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You are not here to think about what you are worthy of, Pip. You are here to play with me, and you will do it with a smile.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I will not be deterred by your humility, Pip. I will show you games, and you will learn to play them, with Estella as your partner.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I don't think it would be proper, Miss Havisham, for me to play games with Estella when I don't even know her, and I'm not sure I'm worthy of your company, either.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will play with Estella, Pip, and you will do it now. I will not be ignored, and I will not be disappointed.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You dare to question my judgment, Pip? I know exactly what I am doing, and you will do as I say, or you will leave my house at once.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I wouldn't wish to play games that might cause any trouble, Miss Havisham. I'm just a poor boy, and I don't want to cause any inconvenience to you or your estate.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I don't know how to play these games, Miss Havisham, and I fear I might make a fool of myself, which would be most unbecoming.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will learn, Pip, and you will play. I will instruct Estella, and together, you will amuse me.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I will not have you sulking and making excuses, Pip. You will go and change into something suitable for playing, at once.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.
